title: A New Way to Spot a Tricky Quantum Link
summary:
Quantum teleportation sounds like science fiction, but it does not beam people or objects across a room. Instead, it moves quantum information from one place to another. It uses a strange link called entanglement to do this.

Here is the weird part about entanglement. Particles such as photons, which are tiny bits of light, can become so deeply linked that scientists cannot describe them separately. The whole system has to be treated as one thing. The idea famously troubled Albert Einstein.

To build future technologies, scientists need to figure out which type of entangled state they have made. One important type is called a W state. Scientists already had a one-shot way to identify another type, called the GHZ state. But no comparable method had been proposed or tested in an experiment for the W state.

Researchers at Kyoto University and Hiroshima University set out to fill that gap. They used a pattern in the W state called cyclic shift symmetry. In simple terms, the photons can be shifted in a repeating cycle while an important underlying pattern stays the same.

"More than 25 years after the initial proposal concerning the entangled measurement for GHZ states, we have finally obtained the entangled measurement for the W state as well, with genuine experimental demonstration for 3-photon W states," said corresponding author Shigeki Takeuchi.

The team built a device and sent three photons into it. It could tell different types of three-photon W states apart. The researchers say the idea could help with quantum communication and quantum computing in the future.
why_it_matters: It could help scientists build future tools for quantum communication and quantum computing.
